summary: The TASK-101 through TASK-106 train is approval-ready and correctly prioritizes submission evidence over more setup: evaluation selection, better generated CARLA evidence, prompt-to-scenario generation, Alpamayo+RAG comparison, Fail2Drive extension framing, and final packaging.

finding_log.summary: TASK-104 depends on live RunPod availability; the plan contains a fallback to planned/blocked records, but the final submission will be substantially stronger if at least one additional memory-pair inference lands.
evidence: TASK-104 Autonomy Readiness names RunPod/HF availability as the main gate
TASK-106 can package partial/blocked rows if upstream evidence is missing

rubric_sections.name: spec-contract
findings: The sequence maps directly to the SoTA requirements: simulation environment, randomized generation, model behavior, realistic latency, failure analysis, and final deliverables.
Lower-signal work such as stock Fail2Drive scoring, Meshy, SimLingo, and serving acceleration is explicitly deprioritized.
rubric_sections.next_action: Approve the train and implement serially in TASK-101 -> TASK-106 order.

rubric_sections.name: implementation-plan
findings: Each ticket has file maps, signature deltas, typed flow, acceptance criteria, verification, and autonomy readiness.
The order reduces drift: select cases first, improve video, add prompt studio, run VLA/RAG, attach Fail2Drive reference, then package.
rubric_sections.next_action: Begin with TASK-101; do not skip directly to more live inference before the matrix exists.

rubric_sections.name: evidence-quality
findings: Planned artifacts are concrete and map to final claims.
The plans preserve claim boundaries around open-loop Alpamayo and generated simulator evidence.
rubric_sections.next_action: During implementation, keep proof rows labeled proved/partial/blocked to avoid the overclaim pattern logged in TROUBLES.

next_action: Implement TASK-101 through TASK-106 as the final submission-focused batch.
